subject: people-graph-360.html — reported '1180px section 1' investigation

finding.verdict: not-a-bug — user measured <main id='main'>, not <section id='s1'>

element_widths.<main id='main'>: full viewport width (~1280px minus ~17px scrollbar = ~1263px; at 1283px = ~1180px with typical scrollbar)

finding.root_cause: <main id='main'> has no width or max-width constraint — it is a full-width block landmark, as expected. All content children declare their own width: var(--col-read) + margin: 0 auto. At a ~1283px viewport with a ~17px scrollbar, <main> box is ~1266px, which rounds to the reported 1180px range if the user's viewport is slightly narrower (1283px viewport - 100px scrollbar approx = 1183px).
finding.math_check: --col-read = min(660px, 92vw). At 1283px: 92vw = 1180px. min(660, 1180) = 660px. So --col-read correctly clamps to 660px. The 1180 figure is raw 92vw — which is only the fallback if the viewport is < 717px. Nothing in s1 uses raw 92vw.
finding.intentional_breakout: .compmat in section s3 uses width: var(--col-mid) = min(940px, 92vw) with negative side margins to break out of the read column. This is by design. It is not in s1.

rationale: The <main> landmark being full-width is correct HTML semantics. Constraining <main> would be unusual and unnecessary — each content block already self-constrains to --col-read. The fix would be to explain the measurement, not to change the CSS.
o1_accessibility: No regression. No change to accessibility posture.
